previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for management of congestive heart failure with a history of acute on chronic diastolic dysfunction and constrictive physiology confirmed on prior right heart catheterization. She presented with volume overload, bilateral lower extremity edema, and dyspnea on exertion. Hypokalemia was present on admission with a potassium of 2.8, requiring discontinuation of furosemide and initiation of potassium repletion. IV and oral electrolyte replacement improved potassium to safe levels, allowing cautious restart of diuretics. The patient struggled with adherence to fluid and sodium restrictions, which impeded diuresis. She reported significant emotional distress following her mother's recent death and expressed difficulty coping with treatment limitations. Despite medical recommendations, she chose to leave the hospital against medical advice before completing the diuresis plan or undergoing a scheduled cardiac MRI. Discharge was to home with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and avoid restarting diuretics without potassium monitoring.

#) Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure: The patient has 
constrictive heart failure as determined by a recent R heart 
catheterization. Pt presented with chest pain/pressure, SOB, and 
evidence of volume overload in the setting of 2 recent 
admissions with incomplete diuresis. Her acute decompensation on 
this admission was felt to be secondary to incomplete diuresis 
on her previous admissions. She was 68 lbs over her dry weight. 
CXR was consistent with volume overload and she had significant 
___ edema. No increased O2 requirement. She was aggressively 
diuresed with 19L removed over the course of her stay. She 
remained ~40 lbs above her reported dry weight on discharge, 
however appeared euvolemic clinically. She will follow-up with 
Dr. ___ as an outpatient. Could also consider a cardiac MR 
to further evaluate her CHF.
.
#) Chest pain: Most likely related to CHF exacerbation. EKG with 
no ischemic changes and CE neg x 2. CP was reproducible on exam 
and was not improved with SLN or morphine, all making ACS less 
likely. Additionally, she had had a cath on ___ which 
revealed clean coronaries.

#) AMS: Pt was initially very somnolent. ABG consistent with 
chronic CO2 retention, likely multifactorial due to obesity 
hypoventilation, COPD, OSA. Mental status improved to normal. 
Likely related to decreased sleep and recent stress as well as 
possibly the morphine she received in the ED.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with volume overload from 
heart failure causing chest pressure. You were diuresed 
successfully with IV and the oral lasix and 20 lbs of fluid were 
removed. Your weight at discharge is 339 lbs. You should 
continue to take lasix 80mg by mouth daily at home. Once you 
have a scale at home, weigh yourself daily. If you notice that 
your weight increases by more than 2 lbs in one day, you should 
call your doctor for instructions on how to increase your lasix 
dose. You should keep a low salt diet restricted to no more than 
2g of sodium per day. You should also limit your fluid intake to 
1.5-2L per day.
.
Note you have been started on three new medications. Aspirin and 
metoprolol for your heart and iron to treat your iron deficiency 
anemia.
.
Please take all other medications as prescribed and keep all 
scheduled follow-up appointments.
.
If you develop chest pain, shortness of breath, or fevers > 101, 
you should return to the emergency room.
